descripcion: At B2 feedback names what happened and what to change, kept separate from a judgement of character. The full four-slot structure with an acknowledged limit (C1) isn't the target yet — describing behaviour and suggesting a change clearly is enough.

filas: The report had a few mistakes in it.
Maybe double-check the numbers next time.

ejemplos.texto: The report had a few mistakes in the numbers.
Maybe it would help to double-check before sending it.
Can I give you some quick feedback on that?

notas: Asking permission first (can I give you some feedback?) makes the rest much easier to accept.
Describing behaviour instead of character avoids sounding like a personal attack.
One suggestion at a time is more useful than a long list of everything that could be improved.

es.en: Spanish can separate the action from the person (el informe tenía errores – the report had some errors, rather than eres descuidado – you're careless). English feedback relies on exactly this separation, so the action-focused form is worth using consistently.
es.es: El español puede separar la acción de la persona («el informe tenía errores» – «the report had some errors», en lugar de «eres descuidado» – «you're careless»). El feedback en inglés depende precisamente de esa separación, por lo que conviene usar de forma sistemática la formulación centrada en la acción.

de.en: German uses the same separation (der Bericht hatte einige Fehler rather than du bist schlampig), and ehrlich gesagt corresponds to to be honest. Constructive feedback therefore transfers directly.
de.de: Im Deutschen trennt man ebenfalls Sache und Person («der Bericht hatte einige Fehler» statt «du bist schlampig»), und «ehrlich gesagt» entspricht «to be honest». Konstruktives Feedback lässt sich daher direkt übertragen.

it.en: Italian uses the same separation (nel rapporto c'erano degli errori rather than sei distratto), so constructive feedback transfers directly.
it.it: L'italiano usa la stessa separazione («nel rapporto c'erano degli errori» invece di «sei distratto»), quindi il feedback costruttivo si trasferisce direttamente.

fr.en: French uses the same separation (le rapport contenait quelques erreurs rather than tu es négligent), so constructive feedback transfers directly.
fr.fr: Le français utilise la même séparation («le rapport contenait quelques erreurs» plutôt que «tu es négligent»), donc le feedback constructif se transfère directement.

pt.en: Portuguese uses the same separation (o relatório tinha alguns erros rather than és descuidado), so constructive feedback transfers directly.
pt.pt: O português usa a mesma separação («o relatório tinha alguns erros» em vez de «você é descuidado»), então o feedback construtivo se transfere diretamente.

errores: Judging character instead of describing behaviour: you're disorganised instead of the files weren't labelled clearly.
Giving feedback without asking permission first.
Giving several pieces of feedback at once instead of focusing on one.

autochequeo: Is the feedback about behaviour, not character?
Was permission asked before giving feedback?
Is only one main point given, not a long list?
Is there a clear, specific suggestion for next time?
Would the other person know exactly what to change?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on how the feedback is given. Check whether it describes behaviour rather than character, and whether it includes a specific, actionable suggestion. Do not rewrite the text.

de: Carrying over German directness: *This is wrong* with no cushioning, which is neutral in German but sounds harsh in English.
